original_post_text:
They Sent Undercover Agents to Play $1/$2… and THIS is What They Came Up With? 😂 

By now you’ve seen the headlines. The Lodge Card Club in Round Rock is dark. Assets frozen. Hundreds of employees displaced. And after a nine-month undercover investigation, six covert visits, bank records, the IRS, and a 22-page affidavit, the biggest charge they could build rests largely on… large deposits from a cash business and one agent who got Lucky to play without a membership.

“Call the floor because we need a new setup”.

Now let me be clear, nobody has been charged with anything. No arrests have been made. And in America, you are innocent until proven guilty. But when you stack this situation up against the 2019 Houston raids on Post Oak Poker Club and Prime Social, where nine people were actually arrested and $10 million was frozen, and all of those charges were eventually dropped, you start to wonder exactly what standard is being applied here.

One thing is certain. Competition in Texas poker is fierce. On the felt AND off the felt.

The Lodge San Antonio? Still open. Same company. Same ownership. Make that make sense.

Texas poker has always survived on skill, resilience, and community. The rooms are still running across DFW and the games are good. But stories like this remind us that the legal landscape in this state remains grey by design.

We’re watching this one closely.

The ShamGod Poker Report is coming soon, where we cover Texas poker the way it deserves to be covered. Real analysis. Real talk. No fluff. Stay locked in.

Full article linked below. Read it and drop your thoughts.

Originally posted March 17, 2026.

When I first read the March 17 update on the TABC search-warrant affidavit regarding The Lodge, I almost didn't want to give my opinion right away — I needed a moment to calm down first, because something about this looked really, really fishy.

Once I sat down with the details, one question stood out: They sent undercover agents to play $1/$2… and THIS is what they came up with?

By now you've seen the headlines. The Lodge Card Club in Round Rock is dark. Assets frozen. Hundreds of employees displaced. And after a nine-month undercover investigation, six covert visits, bank records, the IRS, and a 22-page affidavit, the biggest case they could build rests largely on large deposits from a cash business and one agent who got lucky enough to play without a membership.

"Call the floor because we need a new setup."

Now let me be clear: nobody has been charged with anything. No arrests have been made. And in America, you are innocent until proven guilty. But when you stack this situation up against the 2019 Houston raids on Post Oak Poker Club and Prime Social — where nine people were actually arrested, $10 million was frozen, and all of those charges were eventually dropped — you start to wonder exactly what standard is being applied here.

One thing is certain: competition in Texas poker is fierce, on the felt AND off the felt.

The Lodge San Antonio? Still open. Same company. Same ownership. Make that make sense.

Texas poker has always survived on skill, resilience, and community. The rooms are still running across DFW and the games are good. But stories like this remind us that the legal landscape in this state remains gray by design.
